root_idea.summary: The root centers on driving or urging something onward.
root_idea.development: From directing animals or people forward, the root develops related uses for things conveyed to a destination, markets as places to which goods are driven, and the ساق as the limb by which a moving creature proceeds. Further extensions include succession, compulsion, and the intensity of a struggle.

senses.definition: To drive or urge people, animals, or other things onward, causing them to proceed toward a destination.
senses.usage_conditions: The Quranic group includes active and passive forms: beings may be driven, or an agent may drive them onward.

senses.definition: The driving or being led onward; in the Quranic expression, the final being brought before one's Lord.
senses.usage_conditions: A verbal noun used in the construction إِلَى رَبِّكَ يَوْمَئِذٍ الْمَسَاقُ, describing the final movement or return to the Lord.

senses.definition: A driver or one who drives another onward; in the Quranic scene, the one who brings a person to the place of assembly and judgment.
senses.usage_conditions: An active participle functioning as the agent of سَاقَ. The Quranic context permits an angelic driver, without making the lexical definition dependent on a particular identification of the agent.

senses.definition: The leg or shank, the part of a human or animal limb between the knee and foot or its corresponding portion.
senses.usage_conditions: A literal anatomical noun; the exact portion varies somewhat by the type of creature under discussion.

senses.definition: In التفت الساق بالساق, one leg joined or intertwined with the other at death.
senses.usage_conditions: The Quranic construction is explained literally as the legs being joined when the soul departs, when the body is wrapped in burial cloth, or when the legs can no longer carry it.

senses.definition: In التفت الساق بالساق, the affliction of one state joined to the affliction of another, especially the distress of the present life with that of the final state.
senses.usage_conditions: This is a figurative Quranic interpretation of the same construction, distinct from the literal reference to joined legs.

senses.definition: In يوم يُكْشَفُ عن ساق, an image of intense difficulty, calamity, or a crisis revealed.
senses.usage_conditions: The expression is idiomatic rather than a claim that a physical shank is literally exposed; related Classical Arabic idioms use the shank for a situation becoming severe.

senses.definition: A market or marketplace, a place to which merchandise is brought for commerce.
senses.usage_conditions: The Quranic occurrences include the plural أَسْوَاقٌ, markets.

senses.definition: The plural of سَاقٌ: legs or shanks.
senses.usage_conditions: In the Quranic plural form, the word refers to legs in the description of the legs of animals or people.

senses.definition: Stems or trunks of plants, an extended use of سَاقٌ and its plural.
senses.usage_conditions: The Quranic plant image uses the plural in the sense of stems supporting branches.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To compel or command people by exercising mastery over them; idiomatically, to press someone to intercede.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Figurative extensions of driving, including forceful or tyrannical command and urging someone to seek another's intercession.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To impel or bring someone toward what has been destined for him, also said of desire or a similar force.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative use in which destiny or an inward impulse is treated as the driver.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To send, convey, or cause something to reach another person, especially a dowry; also to cause good fortune to befall someone.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The construction with إِلَى marks the recipient or destination. The dowry use is an extension from the historical practice of driving animals as bride-price.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To cause a rivulet or watercourse to run toward a piece of land.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A causative extension of directing something along a course.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To carry on a narrative, discourse, or course of affairs.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used of arranging or prosecuting speech or affairs in a continuing course.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A rhetorical presentation of what is known in the manner of asking about what is unknown, producing hyperbolic emphasis.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A named rhetorical mode derived from carrying one expression along as though it belonged to another category.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of a sick person, to give up the soul, approach death, or undergo the agony of dying.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The reflexive or prepositional construction may describe the person whose soul is being expelled rather than an agent driving another.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To strike or hurt another person's shank.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A separate transitive use with the shank as the object.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To drive thoroughly, vigorously, or well.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A Form II intensification of the driving action.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To make someone take charge of, or exercise authority over, his affair.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative Form II construction concerning the management or ordering of a matter.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of a plant or tree, to have a stem, stock, or trunk.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A Form II denominative use derived from سَاقٌ in the sense of plant stem.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To vie or compete with another in driving, strength, or keeping pace.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A reported additional explanation gives the sense “to follow”; the central attested branch concerns rivalry or matching another's exertion.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The making of things consecutive or successive, as though one portion drove another onward.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A noun associated with the Form III reciprocal construction.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To make someone drive camels, give him camels to drive, or figuratively make him possess camels.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The construction may emphasize assigning the task of driving or the resulting possession.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To trade in a market, buying and selling.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A Form V use associated with activity in the market.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of camels, sheep, or goats, to follow one another or press onward in succession.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The animals are depicted as driving one another forward, sometimes because of weakness or leanness.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of two marriage proposals, to occur simultaneously.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A legal usage is reported, but its status is explicitly disputed in the lexical tradition.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To go along while being driven, or to drive oneself along; of camels, to become consecutive.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A quasi-passive Form VII use, with a secondary extension to succession.

other_classical_meanings.definition: In idioms, to prepare oneself for difficulty, to become active and apply oneself vigorously, or for a battle to become severe; a reported expression also means nearly accomplishing an intended action.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: These are figurative and idiomatic extensions of the shank imagery, not additional anatomical senses. The interpretation of أَوْهَتْ بِسَاقٍ is reported with some uncertainty.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A greave or other covering worn on the shank.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A secondary object-based application of the anatomical noun.

other_classical_meanings.definition: In expressions such as سَاقًا عَلَى سَاقٍ, one after another; also arranged in a single row or series.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An idiomatic use derived from the successive movement or alignment of legs and stems.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The soul or self; in a related idiom, one's essential self or honor may be harmed or impugned.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative use in expressions such as قَدَحَ فِي سَاقِهِ, whose interpretation ranges from damaging the soul to damaging reputation.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The male of a species of collared turtle-dove, also identified with the warshān.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This is a fixed lexical bird name and is not the ordinary anatomical noun in context.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Merchandise or trade.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A metonymic use of the market noun, referring to the goods or commerce associated with it.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The thickest, most vehement, or central part of a battle.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative compound referring to the core of combat.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Length or beauty of the shanks.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A descriptive noun concerning the form or appearance of the legs.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The rear or hindmost part of an army or traveling company, whose members drive and guard those ahead.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A collective or positional military term derived from the act of driving from behind.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A subject or subjects of a king, as opposed to a ruler.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used alike for singular and plural, and for masculine and feminine; it does not mean market people.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The part of the plant called ṭurthūth located below its head or upper portion.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized botanical term.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of or relating to a market; a market person or market people.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The plural سُوقِيُّونَ denotes people associated with the market.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A hide described as prepared or dressed, or alternatively as unprepared or undressed.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The lexical tradition records disagreement over which condition the adjective denotes; the second explanation is reported as more common.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A meal or gruel made from parched barley, wheat, or other grains and mealy foods.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: It may be moistened and sipped or eaten dry; the term also has dialectal variants.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Wine, literally “the sawīq of the vine.”
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A distinct lexical use from the ordinary parched-grain food.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A dowry or nuptial gift.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A substantive use of the verbal noun, connected historically with conveying animal bride-price.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The following part, context, drift, thread, or tenor of a discourse.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Opposed to سِبَاقٌ, the preceding portion; it may also describe the course or scope of affairs.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A seller or maker of sawīq.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A professional noun derived from سَوِيقٌ, not the intensive driver noun.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Long in the shank; of a plant, having a stem.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The adjective is applied to persons for long shanks and figuratively or descriptively to plants with stems.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Having a stem or stock, said of a plant.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A botanical adjectival use.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The emerging spadix of a palm tree when it has grown to about a span in length.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized botanical term.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Clouds driven along by the wind.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The clouds may be described as containing water or as dry, depending on the usage reported.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Beasts or camels driven away together, especially by an enemy or pursuing horsemen.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A collective noun for animals being driven as a group.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A person impelled by destiny toward what has been allotted to him.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative expression presenting destiny as the driver.

other_classical_meanings.definition: An animal used by a hunter as concealment or a decoy while approaching game.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The animal is driven toward the quarry so that the hunter can conceal himself and shoot.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Having long, thick, or beautiful shanks; applied to a man, with سَوْقَاءُ for a woman.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An adjective describing the form or appearance of the shanks.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The strap of a horse's stirrup.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized equestrian term.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A camel that vies with game in driving onward or strength, or a camel used to help conceal a hunter from game.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The lexical explanations differ between a vigorous pursuing camel and one used as a hunting device.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A staff or stick used to drive cattle.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A concrete instrument noun; the entry is noted as possibly post-Classical.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A follower or servant, literally one who is driven along.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative passive-participial use.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A relation or near kinsman.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A separate figurative use recorded for the same form.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A mountain extending lengthwise along the surface of the earth.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A descriptive compound using the idea of something drawn out or extended along a course.

lane_unit_coverage.note: Driving clouds is covered by the general Quranic driving sense.
Reported additional sense is retained in the target usage conditions.
Lexical disagreement is retained in usage conditions.
Inflectional cross-reference describing the verbal noun.

cautions: The Quranic سَاقٌ passages support both literal anatomical readings and established idiomatic readings involving death or severe difficulty; these are kept as separate senses and constructions.
The public form سُوقٌ combines the market noun with Quranic plural uses of سَاقٌ, including legs and plant stems; the homographic senses are distinguished explicitly.
